text:
REVIEW OF OPERATIONS
DUBBO PROJECT
During the year, ASM made a transformative shift in the Dubbo Project’s development approach with the release of its
Heap Leach Scoping Study.” The Scoping Study is part of the Company’s Rare Earth Options Assessment (REOA) — a
strategic initiative to identify lower capital, shorter implementation pathways to rare earth production.
KOREAN METALS PLANT
The KMP has been in commercial production of light rare earth metals and alloys since 2022, with the facility now
producing neodymium (Nd) and neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) metals and a range of neodymium praseodymium
iron boron (NdFeB) alloys for
a growing number of global customers.
Safety
There were no reportable safety incidents recorded at the KMP during the year, with the Lost Time Injury Frequency
Rate remaining at zero.
Production and sales
During the year, ASM prioritised NdFeB alloy production, given its more favourable margin profile, and achieved a
positive increase in delivery volumes. Across the 12 months ending 30 June 2026, the KMP dispatched:
e
NdFeB alloy:
~116 tonnes
e — NdPr metal:
~33 tonnes
Phase 2 expansion
With increased sales agreements, growing capability and positive market momentum, ASM commenced Phase 2
expansion activities at the KMP during the year.
Phase 2 ramp-up plans will lift NdFeB alloy nameplate production capacity from ~1,300tpa to ~3,600tpa.
Heavy rare earth development
During the year, ASM achieved its first commercial sale of terbium (Tb) and dysprosium (Dy) metals, produced at the
KMP and sold to Neo Performance Materials. This milestone represents a critical step in developing a secure, non-
China supply of heavy rare earth metals — a capability held by only a handful of producers globally.
AMERICAN METALS PLANT
ASM’s plan to establish a metals and alloys plant in the US (American Metals Plant or AMP) is well advanced and has
been central to the Company’s strategy.
